description:
Hi there!

Just tying to park a multi-billion-dollar spacecraft at the Moon's South Pole where there's no GPS, massive craters block the Sun, and Earth's Wi-Fi keeps dropping behind a mountain—without accidentally creating a new crater. What could possibly go wrong?

You will soon find out how 'easy' it actually is when landing one yourself.
summary: LUNAR ODYSSEY is a mobile-first lunar landing site navigation and simulation application. It helps users explore and compare potential Moon landing locations by examining terrain, sunlight availability, solar power potential and Earth communication visibility. It combines an interactive mission planner with a 3D lunar landing simulation and surface exploration experience. The project makes important lunar mission-planning concepts accessible to students, educators and future mission planners.
details:
LUNAR ODYSSEY — Lunar Landing Site Navigator

Problem

Selecting a lunar landing site requires evaluating several important factors, including terrain, sunlight availability for solar power and visibility of Earth for direct communication. These factors can affect mission safety and operations.

Solution

LUNAR ODYSSEY is a mobile-first interactive lunar exploration and mission-planning application. It allows users to explore lunar locations, compare candidate landing sites, analyze Sun and Earth visibility, estimate solar energy potential and experience a simulated lunar landing.

Main Features

  • Compare two potential lunar landing sites.
  • Analyze sunlight availability and estimated solar energy potential.
  • Estimate Earth visibility for potential communication windows.
  • Use local terrain horizon information to account for obstructions.
  • Choose mission priorities: Balanced, Sun Power or Earth Visibility.
  • Experience an interactive 3D lunar landing simulation.
  • Explore the lunar surface after landing.
  • Capture a downloadable lunar exploration photograph.
  • Generate a downloadable mission report.

Data and Methodology

The application uses lunar terrain information derived from NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) elevation data to generate local horizon profiles for two example sites.

It also incorporates JPL Horizons DE441 topocentric ephemeris data for the Sun and Earth at the two example lunar locations for November 14, 2026.

Solar energy estimates consider direct sunlight, terrain obstruction, solar panel area, efficiency and orientation. Earth visibility is estimated using its elevation relative to the local terrain horizon and a configurable minimum antenna elevation.

Impact

LUNAR ODYSSEY makes lunar mission-planning concepts easier to explore through an interactive mobile experience. It helps users understand how sunlight, terrain and Earth visibility influence the selection of lunar landing locations.

Limitations

This is an educational and exploratory prototype, not a certified landing-safety or engineering system. The solar-energy model does not include every real-world electrical, thermal or hardware effect. Communication visibility is a geometric estimate, not a verified radio link budget. High-precision ephemeris datasets are included for two example sites and one date; other dates or locations may use an approximate offline model unless matching datasets are imported.

Project Links

Live application: https://iammsarim.github.io/lunar-odyssey/

Source code: https://github.com/IamMSarim/lunar-odyssey/
